chapters.summary: Over six days God creates the heavens, the earth, and everything in them, then makes humanity in his own image and blesses the seventh day as a day of rest.
keyPoints: God creates order and life out of formless emptiness, revealing his great power.
God makes humanity in his own image, giving people dignity and responsibility to govern all creation.
God sees everything he has made as very good, and sets apart the seventh day as holy.
chapters.application: We should approach nature with reverence, treasure life, and keep rest even in busyness, remembering God's creation and care.

chapters.summary: This chapter describes God resting after completing creation, and details the forming of Eden and of Adam and Eve, along with the institution of marriage.
keyPoints: God rests on the seventh day and blesses it as holy, setting an example of rest for humanity.
God forms the man from the dust of the ground and breathes life into him; he becomes a living being.
God plants Eden and makes a companion for the man, establishing the pattern of marriage between one man and one woman.
chapters.application: In the busyness of life, we should follow God's example of resting after creating, refocusing on him — and treasure marriage, sustaining it with love and faithfulness.

chapters.summary: Tempted by the serpent, the first man and woman disobey God's command and eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; after sinning they hide from God, face judgment, and are driven from Eden.
keyPoints: The serpent cunningly casts doubt on God's word, tempting Eve to question his command.
Humanity disobeys and eats the forbidden fruit; sin enters the world, bringing shame and the impulse to shift blame.
God pronounces judgment, but also promises that the woman's offspring will crush the serpent's head — a hope of redemption.
chapters.application: When temptation comes, hold fast to God's word instead of following our own judgment; when we fall, confess honestly and trust in God's forgiveness and rescue.
